name: termeleon
description: Read the color schemes already installed for Ghostty, kitty, Alacritty, WezTerm, iTerm2, Windows Terminal and Xresources, and apply them to the VS Code integrated terminal.

commands.title: Import Terminal Theme to User Settings…
Import Terminal Theme to Workspace Settings…

termeleon.target.markdownDescription: Where to write the imported palette. `ask` prompts each time; with no folder open it always uses user settings.

termeleon.sources.description: Emulators to scan. Empty means all of them.

termeleon.extraDirectories.description: Additional directories to sweep for theme files, e.g. a dotfiles checkout.

termeleon.scopeToActiveTheme.markdownDescription: Nest the colors under `[Your Theme Name]` so they only apply while that workbench theme is active. Off by default, so the terminal palette survives theme switching.

termeleon.setMinimumContrastRatio.markdownDescription: Also set `#terminal.integrated.minimumContrastRatio#` to 1. Without this, VS Code adjusts foreground colors toward a contrast target and the palette will not render as authored.

termeleon.includeSelectionForeground.markdownDescription: Write `terminal.selectionForeground`. Off by default: setting it disables the behavior where selected text keeps its own color.

termeleon.livePreview.description: Apply each theme as you arrow through the list, and restore your previous colors if you cancel. Turn off if the settings.json churn is disruptive.

scripts.pretest:host: npm run compile && npm run compile-tests
scripts.test: npm run test:parsers && npm run test:host
